phase: 6 - host rehearsal of the write path
where: host only; the phone was not touched this round
writer: bsd/miscfs/apfs/apfs_write.c apfs_write_in_place(), the kernel's own; it had no caller until now

image.contents: sub/target.bin 12288 bytes (3 blocks), sub/other.bin 8192 bytes, both random because mkapfs compresses anything compressible into an attribute

steps.name: write
steps.result: write_in_place -> 0, first=96 blocks=1 bytes=4096 partial=0 calls=1
steps.verdict: MATCH after rereading with the cache flushed

steps.name: blast radius
steps.result: exactly one block of the 4 MiB image differs: block 96
steps.means: the container superblock, both object maps, the fs tree and every other file are byte-identical

steps.name: torn write
steps.result: after halving the block, the volume still opens, the inode reads, and the file reads 12288 bytes
steps.means: the loss is a mixture of old and new contents, not a damaged filesystem

steps.name: recovery
steps.result: rewriting the original contents through the same writer returns the image byte-identical to the original
steps.detail: restore write -> 0 blocks=3; difference from the original image: none

host_build_notes: apfs_lib.h needs <time.h>; a prelude header supplies it
Ubuntu defines ARCH_X86_64, which makes libdeflate look for x86/decompress_impl.h -- a directory this kernel tree does not have. Patched in a temporary copy only; the kernel sources were not changed.
SHA256 is the kernel crypto library and is stubbed; the rehearsal uses an unsealed volume so the stub is never reached
not_done: writing on the phone: no dedicated test space, backup or independent read-back path yet
sync: every block is read back and compared as it goes out, but there is no fsync semantics
